title: A source a refresh read by hand is dated through one census.py read command, not a scratch census log
goal: census.py read ID... --note TEXT --date D dates each named source a person or agent read on its current page as confirmed: it writes the census log row a census writes (outcome confirmed, the note as outcome_note) and runs the confirm step on it, so the source row, the citing articles and the fetch state are dated as census.py confirm dates them, with no scratch census log

run:
import csv, io, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbid, kbroot, kbcommon
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
d = os.path.join(t, "zq")
url = "https://example.org/docs/page"
sid = kbid.source_id(url, "ZQ")
art = ["---", "topic: win/a", "priority: P1", "applies_to: x", "retrieved_utc: 2026-01-01", "sources: [" + sid + "]", "status: complete", "---", "", "# A", "",
       "## Summary", "- Summary line one. [DOC " + sid + "]", "", "## Facts", "- The setting is on by default. [DOC " + sid + "]", ""]
files = {"_root.md": kbroot.root_md("zq", "ZQ", "internal", "planted"), **{k: v.format(name="zq") for k, v in kbroot.FILES.items()}, "win/a.md": "\n".join(art)}
files["_sources.csv"] += sid + "," + url + ",Page,Example Org,CC BY 4.0,quote,2026-01-01,ms.date 2026-01-01,,win/a.md,\n"
cols = kbcommon.STATE_COLS
files["_fetch_state.csv"] = ",".join(cols) + "\n" + ",".join({"id": sid, "url": url, "etag": "W/planted", "detected_utc": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}.get(c, "") for c in cols) + "\n"
for rel, text in files.items():
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(d, rel)) or d, exist_ok=True)
    open(os.path.join(d, rel), "w", newline="").write(text)
env = dict(os.environ, KB_ROOTS=d)
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/census.py", "--root", "zq", "read", sid, "--note", "read the page, the one fact holds", "--date", "2026-06-01"],
                   env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
rows = {x["id"]: x for x in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(open(os.path.join(d, "_sources.csv"), newline="").read()))}
row = rows[sid]
logs = [os.path.join(d, "_census", n) for n in os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "_census"))] if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "_census")) else []
logged = [x for p in logs for x in csv.DictReader(open(p, newline="")) if x.get("id") == sid and x.get("outcome") == "confirmed" and "the one fact holds" in x.get("outcome_note", "")]
bad = []
if row["retrieved_utc"] != "2026-06-01" or "confirmed 2026-06-01: read the page" not in row["version_or_date"]:
    bad.append("source row not dated as confirmed")
if "retrieved_utc: 2026-06-01" not in open(os.path.join(d, "win/a.md")).read():
    bad.append("article not re-dated")
if not logged:
    bad.append("no census log row")
print("read exit", r.returncode, r.stderr[-150:], bad)
sys.exit(1 if r.returncode or bad else 0)

gates.question: Which file does census.py read write its census log rows to?
options: _census/read-<date>.csv of the root, rows of one day added to the file
gates.recommendation: _census/read-<date>.csv of the root, rows of one day added to the file
gates.reason: the full census log name is a census's own, and confirm over a log with other OK rows would date them too
gates.answer: _census/read-<date>.csv of the root, rows of one day added to the file

gates.question: Which roots does census.py read accept for --root?
options: any served root, KB_ROOTS roots included, for read only
only the roots of this repository's kb/, as every other command
gates.recommendation: any served root, KB_ROOTS roots included, for read only
gates.reason: it runs no git, and the goal's check plants its root through KB_ROOTS
gates.answer: any served root, KB_ROOTS roots included, for read only

notes: Found 2026-11-09 when a refresh run had to write a scratch census log and run census.py confirm to date 8 sources it had read by hand. Premise: the planted-root check exits 1 on 55dde769f (census.py has no read subcommand). Lives in census.py (factdiff.py cannot import census); the log goes to _census/ of the root.
